points.description: States the core idea: SVM is a (linear) classifier that separates classes with a decision boundary (hyperplane) chosen to maximise the margin.
points.partial_credit: Half if it mentions a decision boundary/separating classes but not maximum margin (or vice versa).

points.description: Mentions support vectors (the data points closest to the boundary that determine the margin) and/or kernels for non-linearly separable data (optionally quadratic programming).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely refers to points near the boundary or to handling non-linear data, without the terms.

rubric.notes: Full marks: the answer says SVM separates classes with a maximum-margin decision boundary, and mentions support vectors or kernels in any wording. Part marks: a vague answer, e.g. just "separates classes with a line" or only naming one idea loosely. No marks for wrong or off-topic answers. Extra remarks do not lose marks unless they contradict the core idea.
